correctness.rationale: The graph has exact distance set {0,1,2}. On the full zero-sum space, adjacency has middle-contrast eigenvalue 0, antisymmetric eigenvalues (-1±sqrt5)/2 and symmetric generalized eigenvalues satisfying (m+4)lambda^2+(3m+2)lambda-5m=0. Exhaustive sector dimensions m-1+2+2=m+3. For m>=3 the negative root -t_m is strictly smaller than all competing eigenvalues. The powered-distance maximum is exactly (t_m-1)2^p-t_m, proving all p quantifiers, endpoint nullity one and Hilbert ranks. The positive polynomial root monotonicity and simple-root expansion justify the asymptotic; BFS/Jacobi checker replayed but is only supplementary.

evidence: For every diameter-two graph with adjacency matrix A, the powered-distance matrix is D_p=2^p(J-I)+(1-2^p)A, a standard identity.
The closest 2024 theta result is the m=2 boundary only (Młotkowski–Skrzypczyk–Wojtylak, Example 7.2, arXiv:2409.17662).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The powered-distance problem is equivalent to finding the least adjacency Rayleigh quotient on the zero-sum space. This identity by itself does not determine that quotient for all m. The new calculation gives the exact polynomial and its unique dominant mode for every generalized-theta graph with at least four paths.

originality.rationale: Known C5 (m=1) and Θ(2,2,3) (m=2) ordinary-QE values are explicitly excluded from novelty; the checked 2024 theta paper defines exactly three paths. No inspected primary source, published record or recoverable own claim implies the exact infinite m>=3 family classification and asymptotic. residual_risks: The full literature and all unindexed/other-language spectral formulations are not exhaustively searchable; an equivalent earlier formula might exist.
The 2026 theta RKHS work was inspected only at accessible scope and excerpt level, but it advertises three-path graphs, a different number of arms.
Some broad diameter-two spectral methods could make the calculation easier without directly presenting the family formula; this does not substantiate a claim of foundational technique novelty.

value.rationale: Natural complete Hilbert-snowflake classification for generalized theta graphs with m>=3, with a unique critical obstruction, strict deterioration with parallel two-edge paths, a nonzero limiting exponent and exact first asymptotic correction. Ordinary QE non-embeddability inherited from Θ(2,2,3) does not imply these quantitative thresholds or dimensions. The fact is a self-contained two-pole network invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice.
